question: Can a lightweight expert trained on closed-loop testbed logs (observation logs as input, the true shaping rate from the control logs as labels) return estimates close to the true capacity and above the probing envelope's lower bound F on conditions never in the training set?
criterion: Data: observation logs from collector v5 or v6 under local result/staleness, input is add_audio(observation) (same form as fed into the expert library at deployment), label is the rate_kbps of the most recent apply in the control log in the same directory; add a 3-second step exclusion before the first apply; for trace files use only the second-version replay (build appears only once in the control log), exclude the entire trace-replay run of the first-version replay; do not use the smoke directory. Holdout (fixed before running): all runs of the four conditions lowbw_400, paper_high_2000, real_lowbw_01, real_lowbw_05 do not enter training or validation, and are used only for testing; within the training set, split 10% by run number as validation. Model: MLP 150-256-256-1, input scaled according to scripts/lib/encoder0.py, Softplus output in Mbps; loss is asymmetric L1 on the log ratio r=log(estimate/label): 3·max(r,0)+max(−r,0) (overestimation penalized threefold, following the project cost convention); Adam 1e-3, batch 1024, at most 30 epochs, early stopping on validation loss; three seeds (0, 1, 2), deployment takes the seed with the lowest validation loss, rule fixed before running. Criteria (only use closedloop-envelope-echo-v1 switch_env logs with probing envelope records among the holdout runs): (1) under the clear state for lowbw_400 and real_lowbw_01, the median ratio of estimate to label falls within 0.8 to 1.1 for both; (2) in the clear and mild states for both conditions, the fraction of steps where the estimate is above the probing envelope lower bound F is not below 30%. If both are satisfied, holds is recorded and the work proceeds to the second gate (closed-loop batch); if the ratio in any condition is below 0.6 or the fraction is below 10%, does not hold is recorded; otherwise inconclusive. Report only: the same readings for paper_high_2000 and real_lowbw_05; the readings for each of the three seeds; training set and validation set loss; synchronous comparison with the challenge baseline (the switcher's default expert) in the log. Prediction unfavorable to us: the model learns the receiving rate times a constant, so the ratio meets the target but the fraction above F is below 30%. Limitations: only one testbed; labels are shaping rates, and replay matches the trace only at the 5-second scale; for constant-capacity conditions, capacity above the source's 610 kbps cap is unobservable.

verdicts.basis: In the same batch of held-out logs, the challenge baseline (the switcher's default expert) has ratios of 0.342 and 0.203, with above-F proportions of 0.000 and 0.001, and the adapted expert reverses both. Report only: paper_high_2000 ratio 0.584 (capacity above the source cap of 610 kbps is unobservable, estimated at about 1.17 Mbps), above-F proportion 1.0; real_lowbw_05 ratio 0.959, proportion 0.917. The three seeds read consistently (400 kbps ratio 0.99, 0.58 to 0.59 appears only at 2 Mbps). The prediction unfavorable to us did not appear: the above-F proportion far exceeds 30%.
verdicts.limitations: What is held out is the condition rather than the testbed; the label is shaping rate; a proportion above F reaching 90% indicates the model is aggressive, and its freeze cost in closed loop is left to the second gate; at the 2 Mbps condition the estimate is about half the capacity.

question: At the start, each arm's prediction is about twice the receiving rate. Which feature family causes this, and at what magnitude of the latency features does each arm begin to extrapolate and blow up?
criterion: Diagnostic, with no performance criterion for holds or does not hold, only the reading fixed in advance. Main-cause determination: the ratio of the prediction to the receiving rate in the first 5 s of the online call is denoted R_on, and under the same capacity offline it is denoted R_off; if replacing a feature family with its offline median lowers the ratio by no less than half of (R_on − R_off), and at least three of the four arms do so, that family is recorded as the main cause; if no single family satisfies this but replacing all does, it is recorded as multiple families acting jointly; if replacing all also does not satisfy this, the cause lies not in the observed values but in the sequence dynamics, and the first hypothesis recorded earlier that day is rejected. Extrapolation threshold: the smallest Δ such that, after adding Δ to the latency family as a whole on the offline observations, the median of the ratio of prediction to ground truth first exceeds 2.

verdicts.basis: result.json. Two valid findings: 1. E2 on offline observations only sets the packet interval f8 to 0; the ratio of four-arm predictions to ground truth rises from 0.96, 0.98, 1.25, 0.26 to 2.93, 3.12, 1.93, 10.87; setting jitter f9 to 0 or converting packet counts at 978 bytes per packet has little effect. 2. verdicts.limitations: Hypothesis one, recorded earlier that day (traffic-mix mismatch), must be restated: the problem is not the missing audio packets themselves, but that at low bitrates there is often only 1 packet within the window, and the collector records the packet interval as 0 in this case, which does not match the offline definition; this is the tenth collector defect. question: When the encoder no longer performs cross-feature aggregation and aggregation is handled solely by Qwen's attention, how much better is Qwen's three-seed average macro MSE relative to a no-LLM arm that also performs aggregation but uses only mean pooling; is this gain significantly larger than the 0.776% observed when an aggregator is present?
criterion: Fixed before the run; the verdict follows criteria-amendment-v2. Both arms use the existing mt_anchor as base, removing the two-layer cross-feature Transformer aggregator transformer_encoder inside the encoder StateEncoderDualScaleLSTM, keeping only the 15 per-feature dual-scale LSTMs and per-position projection; this change is identical for both arms. The only difference between the two arms is which component performs cross-feature aggregation. Arm A, LLM aggregation: the 15 tokens are fed into Qwen, the last token of last_hidden_state is taken and fed to the original BweHead. Arm B, mean aggregation: the 15 tokens are directly averaged by position to obtain one 1024-dimensional vector, connected to the same BweHead, with no Qwen. Mean pooling is deliberately chosen as the most naive aggregation, containing no learnable cross-token parameters, so that the difference between the two arms is not attributed to other modules. The encoder, BweHead, encoder0, and log_std of the two arms must be bitwise identical; before the run, a pre-check compares the code class block by class block in bwe_agent, with comments stripped; differences are allowed only in the aggregation and LLM segment. The shared protocol is identical to llm-indispensability-mt-anchor-3seed: seeds 0, 1, 2, max_timesteps 50000, the only endpoint is step 50000, eval_freq 5000 is diagnostic only and must not enter adjudication; batch_size 512, buffer_size 3500000, the reward pickle is MRE_4; both arms enable the capacity anchor (capacity_aux_weight 1.0, capacity_huber_delta 1.0); evaluation uses the macro MSE over the 870 calls with the three scenarios equally weighted, and e+ and e− are recorded; leakage-free recheck uses the 712-call subset. The primary adjudication is Arm A relative to Arm B, with four groups according to criteria-amendment-v2: Group A is that the 95% CI of the 870-call stratified paired bootstrap 10000 times with seed 20260909 for seed0 is entirely below 0, and on the 712-call leakage-free subset the direction is the same and the CI is preserved; Group B is that all three seeds are directionally consistent and the 95% confidence interval of the three-seed mean excludes 0 according to a t distribution with 2 degrees of freedom; Group C has two tiers, at least 3% is recorded as a definitive contribution, at least 1.631% is recorded as a reportable positive result; Group D is that macro increase caused by deterioration in any scenario does not exceed 1%. In parallel with the primary adjudication, the amplification adjudication must answer: under this configuration, does the gain of A relative to B simultaneously satisfy being greater than or equal to 1.631% and greater than the measured 0.776% when the aggregator exists. Only if both are satisfied may it be claimed that assigning aggregation solely to the LLM turns it from redundant to necessary; in parallel with the primary adjudication, the spurious-win check adjudication has higher priority than the amplification adjudication and must be answered first: Arm A's own three-seed average macro must not be worse than the measured mt_anchor value 5.449785 when the aggregator exists by more than 3%, that is, must not be higher than 5.613279. If Arm A is worse than this threshold, then regardless of how large A's gain relative to B is, it is adjudicated that the gain comes from weakening the control rather than the LLM becoming stronger, the amplification adjudication directly does not hold, and it must not be used as evidence that the LLM is structurally necessary. The prediction fixed before the run, unfavorable to our goal, must not be changed afterward: removing the encoder's aggregator will weaken both arms simultaneously, Arm A will most likely be worse than 5.449785, so the spurious-win check adjudication has a real risk of failure. The value of this experiment is not that it must succeed, but that it answers directly whether the LLM is structurally necessary. Secondary readings are reported as they are and have no gates: (1) the e+ and e− of the three-seed average of both arms and per-scenario values; (2) the respective changes of Arm A relative to mt_anchor 5.449785 when the aggregator exists and Arm B relative to nollm_mt_anchor 5.492400, used to decompose how the cost of removing the aggregator is distributed between the two arms; (3) following diagnosis-mt-readout-degeneracy in the same way, retest the number of features affecting the output and the number of features entering the readout position for both arms, to see whether the information path changes as expected after removing the aggregator. Criteria are not changed, checkpoints are not selected, and results are not reported only for the favorable arm or seed.

The two arms and their isomorphism were verified call by call before registration and hashes recorded: the LLM arm uses /path/to/server/work/rcaiql_screen_v1/mt_anchor, and the no-LLM arm uses /path/to/server/work/caiql_llm_screen_v2r1/nollm_mt_anchor. Before adjudication these five hashes must be rechecked; if any does not match, the experiment is void. Common protocol: seeds 0, 1, 2, max_timesteps 50000, the only endpoint is step 50000, eval_freq 5000 is diagnostic only and must not enter adjudication or be used for selection; batch_size 512, buffer_size 3500000, reward pickle is MRE_4, both arms enable capacity anchor; evaluation is 870 calls, three scenarios, equal-weight macro MSE, and overestimation e+ and underestimation e− are also recorded; the leakage-free recheck uses the 712-call subset. The pre-registered prediction, whose direction is unfavorable to us, must not be changed afterward: the 20000-step seed0 measurement has LLM better by only 0.776%, below the reportable threshold 1.631%. question: Under the current best configuration with capacity anchor plus 15 tokens, in the same setting of 50000 steps with three seeds, does the version with pretrained weights bring an attributable performance advantage over the randomly initialized, fully trained version of the same architecture?
criterion: Criteria were frozen at 2026-09-13 16:5x CST, at which point randinit_fair had only run a 200-step smoke test, with no 50000-step results; the llm_indispensability output directory on gpu-server-2 was still empty. After this point, no relaxation, no change of control, and no seed or checkpoint selection are permitted. The asymmetry in setup is intentional; its direction is unfavorable to the pretrained arm. The RI arm has 464914450 trainable parameters, 54.7 times the LLM arm's 8496146. That is, random initialization receives the stronger training method. This design is intended to make the conclusion conservative: if the pretrained arm still wins despite the disadvantage of training only LoRA, then the value of pretraining truly holds. The risk in the opposite reading must also be stated: if RI wins, it cannot be distinguished whether "random initialization is good enough" or "full training beats LoRA," as the two are confounded. question: Is the one-token LLM variant locked at about 149 kbps because (a) it outputs too low under online observations at high receiving rates, (b) it never leaves the low-rate region, or (c) some online feature suppresses it?
criterion: Three checks with fixed interpretation rules. A. Cross-replay: feed the online observations left when LLM4Band ramped to high rates into the one-token LLM variant, bin by long-window receiving rate, and look at the ratio of output to receiving rate; replay of its own observations must reproduce the online log (median relative difference less than one percent), otherwise abort. If the median ratio of the one-token LLM variant at each bin above 350 kbps is not below 1.0, judge it as a closed-loop dynamics problem (the model would follow at high rates, it just never reached high rates); if below 0.9, judge it as the model outputting too low under high-rate online observations. B. Startup segment comparison: compare the ratio of output to receiving rate and the sender's actual bitrate for the first 20 seconds of both arms, and find how the two differ in the stretch where LLM4Band ramps up and the one-token LLM variant does not. C. Feature group substitution: at the lock point, replace the 15 feature groups one by one with the values near the same moment from LLM4Band, and record any feature group whose output change exceeds thirty percent as a suspect. Holds if the three checks give a consistent explanation; inconclusive if they contradict each other or are all insignificant. The fix is to be pre-registered separately.

verdicts.basis: Two causes. First, there is a fixed gap of about 25 kbps in the closed loop (from the estimate to the video bitrate), and the estimator with a gain of about 1.2 falls exactly on the critical line near 150 kbps: the one-token LLM variant is slightly below the line online, and LLM4Band is slightly above it. Second, the one-token LLM variant has a valley in its online response in the 200 to 350 kbps range: the ratio of output to receiving rate is only 0.85 to 0.86, whereas LLM4Band is 1.23 to 1.38 under the same observation; on the offline validation set, the two are almost identical in this range (1.08 vs. 1.10), so this valley is induced by the difference between online observations and the training distribution, not something the model has offline. Post hoc probing: the testbed does not report audio packets to the estimator, while the rate-related features in the training data include audio, so the online receiving rate is systematically low by about 41 kbps; after adding it back, the one-token LLM variant's output at the lock point rises from 150 to 176 (required 147), and in the startup segment rises from 158 to 191 (required 169), enough to leave the lock point, but at 225 kbps it is 233 versus the required 250, and the valley remains.
verdicts.limitations: Replay is open-loop; whether it truly unlocks can only be answered by closed-loop. The steady-state response curve is approximated by scaling all rate-type features globally, which is not faithful and was not used as evidence. The audio compensation item is a post hoc probe. Only one run each at the 1000 and 2000 kbps conditions was examined.

question: Under the four held-out foreign schemas, does the closed-loop utility of the LLM mapping approach the error-free as-is case, exceed the no-adaptation case, and exceed the better of distribution matching and name matching?
criterion: See registry/preregistrations/prereg_46.md. Eight windows (four ferry, four bus, previously unused) × 17 conditions, primary endpoint U, the better comparator is the one with the higher mean U among DIST and NAME. A schema is effective if the no-adaptation arm is at least 3 lower than the no-error arm. Holds: at least two effective schemas; for each effective schema the LLM is at least 3 higher than no adaptation, positive in at least 7/8 windows, and no more than 2 below no error; for each schema the LLM is not more than 1 lower than the better comparator; for at least half of the effective schemas (rounded up) the LLM is at least 3 higher than the better comparator. Does not hold: for any effective schema the LLM is not higher than no adaptation, or for any schema it is more than 3 lower than the better comparator, or no effective schema is at least 3 higher than the better comparator. Inconclusive: the rest. An unparseable LLM answer counts as no adaptation. Unfavorable prediction: the LLM gives no answer within the token limit; the errors of the statistical mappings fall on insensitive features, giving ties; the probing envelope makes the no-adaptation loss less than 3 points.

Condition audit: jobs 136, run 136, invalid 4, hard check failures 0, soft check warnings 113; power mode ['performance']; maximum package temperature during runs 99.0°C; decision interval 95th percentile median 85.0993408203125 ms.

revisions.reason: The original criterion had two objective flaws, unrelated to whom the results favor. First, the endpoint used absolute utility, and the better comparator was selected post hoc by highest utility, which is not monotone in what interface adaptation is meant to achieve: a method with item-by-item mapping errors can exceed the error-free original as long as it happens to make the estimator more aggressive (test_c name matching 91.7 vs. error-free 88.6, with mapping errors), so a method that is item-by-item correct and only 0.5 points from error-free is instead judged to lose, and the criterion contradicts "whether adaptation is correct." Second, the multiplicative condition that every schema must pass means noise in a single schema can overturn the outcome. The revision was made after seeing the results; the fidelity endpoint had first been seen in the exploration record obsschema-cl-v1-fidelity-explore. The new criterion was not created for these data; it is identical to the confirmatory criterion registered before the obsschema-closedloop-v2 run and treats the four methods equally.

Holds: interval lower bound > 0 and Δ ≥ 3; direction only: Δ > 0; does not hold: Δ ≤ 0, or the LLM has a cell more than 10 points below same-window error-free. question: With the collector fixed, does the closed loop at 200 kbps and below stop collapsing, and how does the switcher compare with the best single arm and with GCC on each of the three profiles?
criterion: Judged profile by profile; there is no overall criterion. For each profile: S1 requires at least 2 valid runs out of three repetitions of switch_nn; S2 requires the mean utility of switch_nn to be no less than the maximum mean of the valid fixed arms minus 5.27; S3 compares with GCC on perf-v1: a difference of at least 5.27 is better, at most −5.27 is worse, and anything in between is comparable. The verdict is mapped from S1: holds if S1 holds on at least two of the three profiles, inconclusive if on one, does not hold if on none. S2 and S3 are written into the conclusion by scenario. See registry/preregistrations/prereg_57.md for details.

verdicts.basis: From cells.json: all 36 runs valid, 0 collapsed cells, 0 retries. The same three profiles on perf-v1 (old collector) crashed on all nine switch_nn attempts, and the three fixed arms had only 5 valid out of 27 attempts. Under v5, per-arm packet loss dropped from 0.84 to 0.94 down to 0.001 to 0.026 (except Schaferct_retrained), queueing delay dropped from 700 to 1360 ms down to 88 to 246 ms, and the overestimation ratio was 0.
verdicts.limitations: 1. After the crash disappeared, the opposite-direction problem was exposed: switch_nn, Pioneer and Schaferct_public had rate scores of only 0.15 to 0.29 and underestimation ratios of 0.66 to 0.85, meaning the link used only 20% to 30%, a downward self-confirmation: sending less leads to receiving less, the surrogate ground truth becomes lower accordingly, and the conservative arm appears more accurate. Schaferct_retrained had rate scores of 0.46 and 0.51 at 156 and 200 kbps, and at 200 kbps its utility of 70.9 was the highest among all arms, but the switcher switched only 2 times per run and did not switch to it; at 100 kbps, it dropped 52% of packets due to constant overestimation and had utility 20.5. 2. Therefore, under extremely low bandwidth, the switcher currently only matches GCC and does not outperform it. 3. GCC is the Python version and was cited from the previous batch; it was not run concurrently with this batch. 4. The metric is network utility and does not include video quality; there is a single approximately static video source.

question: Can the collector and four-arm switching estimator, rewritten under the offline protocol, remain fully consistent with the offline data protocol under all four layers of testing: synthetic validation, real packet trace replay, offline equivalence, and short closed-loop testing?
criterion: See registry/preregistrations/prereg_61.md. V1 synthetic: slot order, wraparound, f0 units, identity f3-f4+f5=200 with relative error no more than 1e-9, and after D scaling f5 equals D. V2 replay: f0 f1 f2 of new slot 0 match old slot 4 value by value; for runs with baseline no less than 20 milliseconds, f6 no less than 1, f5 no less than 0, and f3 no less than 0 are all 100%; the number of out-of-range dimensions in the new collector distribution must be less than in the old collector, reported dimension by dimension. V3: offline observations are fed directly to the switcher, and per-block selection and output match the offline simulation bit for bit. V4: a closed-loop call of at least 130 seconds with a 20 ms baseline, at least one wraparound with the median difference of f3 no more than 50 milliseconds in the 1 second before and after, median request interval 55 to 65 milliseconds, and at least 40 arm selections with no abnormal exit. Only if all pass is registration of the closed-loop performance experiment allowed.

verdicts.basis: Online closed-loop observations: 149 of 150 dimensions fall within the offline 1% to 99% quantiles; the only out-of-range dimension, f14_s4, is caused by the training-set mean constant overriding the feature. Replay with the old collector gives 33 out-of-range dimensions. The request interval of 66.5 ms is the testbed's inherent cadence: across 37 historical runs of fixed_env with zero computational overhead, the median is 66.2 to 66.6 ms, and the switcher adds only about 0.15 ms. Per-step computation has a median of 5.67 ms and p99 of 9.75 ms; four-arm inference is about 1.2 ms, and the rest is collector feature computation and trace logging. Old deployment defects verified and corrected in this entry: slot order inversion, interval clock not anchored so each packet forms its own interval, latency origin inconsistent with the offline definition, 64-second wraparound unhandled, f11 definition error, and autoclose silently truncating long profiles at 55 seconds.
verdicts.limitations: Request pacing is about 10% slower than the offline nominal 60 ms, affecting the time scale of LSTM-type arms and the switching block length (50 steps ≈ 3.3 s); in the offline data, adjacent steps are not always a one-slot shift (only 18% are exactly one slot), and the offline effective pacing has not yet been quantified. Packet type proportions are still overridden by constants. The calibration basis for the latency origin is inferred from offline statistics; the official definition was not found in the original text. f11 recovers only 87.6%.

question: Does a sliding-window collector stay consistent with the offline window semantics in synthetic, replay, and closed-loop tests, and can tuning bwe_feedback_duration bring the closed-loop cadence to 60 ms?
criterion: See registry/preregistrations/prereg_60.md. W1: synthetic tests of window assignment, and the long window contains the short window. W2: in replay the long window contains the short window in 100% of steps, and the median ratio of long-window to short-window packet counts falls within the offline 5% to 95% quantile range [1.667, 2.274]. W3: fixed_env with settings 50, 55 and 60, 3 runs each; σ is the pooled sample standard deviation, τ=max(3σ,0.5 ms), c*=round((60−a)/b) restricted to the range 30 to 60, and c* is entered in the registry first. W4: switch_nn runs with c* for 140 seconds; all validity checks pass, the median interval differs from 60 by no more than τ, containment is 100%, the median packet-count ratio is within the range, there is at least one wraparound with f3 continuous, and there are at least 40 arm selections. Only if all pass is the closed-loop performance experiment released.

verdicts.basis: The request interval is not controlled by bwe_feedback_duration: under configurations 50, 55, and 60, the median interval across 9 valid runs is between 66.39 and 66.53 milliseconds, the fitted slope is 0.0076, and the run-to-run noise is 0.028 milliseconds. 66.4 milliseconds is close to the 66.67-millisecond frame interval of 15 fps. In the native binary, bandwidth requests are sent by the SendPeriodicFeedbacks path of RemoteEstimatorProxy.
verdicts.limitations: The sliding-window collector itself passes the W1 and W2 checks; what does not hold is the cadence alignment. The containment check of W2 has weak discriminative power, and the main evidence for the sliding window is that 74% of offline adjacent steps cannot be explained by a whole-slot shift.

question: With packet loss counted separately per stream, on the same real packet stream, do the arms stop extrapolating upward?
criterion: Holds if all three pass: (a) the median per-step agreement rate between the short-window packet count replayed by the old collector and the runtime record is not lower than 0.95 (replay timestamps have been corrected by inference latency); (b) the 99th percentile of the long-window packet loss count for v5 is not higher than the offline maximum of 139; (c) for the ratio of whole-run prediction to receiving rate, at least two of the three ONNX arms have a v5-to-v3 ratio no higher than 0.5. Report only: the same ratio for v4 to v3; the median kilobits per second of each arm's prediction after 10 seconds; the MLP arm. Replay is open-loop; closed-loop re-verification is recorded separately after the perf-v1 batch run ends.

verdicts.basis: From replay_result.json, 31 cells. Under the same real packet stream, changing only the packet loss algorithm: after 10 seconds the three ONNX arms' predicted medians drop from 6768, 2056, 7602 kbps to 239, 192, 211 kbps; v4 (fixing only packet intervals) has ratios to v3 of 0.953, 1.05, 0.963, almost no effect. Under the old convention, the long-window packet loss count median is 5714, the 99th percentile is 39734, and the offline maximum is 139.
verdicts.limitations: Open-loop replay: under v5, each arm gives much lower predictions, and in closed loop the sending rate drops accordingly, with far fewer losses and retransmissions, so the whole trace differs and replay cannot reproduce it. The MLP arm predicts a median of 0 under v5, i.e., under heavy loss it drives the call to a standstill; this arm is dangerous at both ends. The full-run ratio for v5 remains 1.24 to 1.59, above 1; whether this is sufficient to avoid queueing at extremely low capacity depends on the closed loop. Scope of impact: in all prior closed-loop runs where retransmission packets appeared, the inputs of the learned arms were contaminated; runs above 400 kbps have very few retransmission packets (17 out of 10165 packets in the v3 native-cadence recheck), so the impact is occasional spikes.

question: In the existing closed-loop runs: is non-video traffic constant per call? Is the video bitrate pinned at the encoder floor when the estimate is below 80 kbps? Does the Python GCC at the 156 and 200 kbps conditions also give estimates in the range where the sender does not respond?
criterion: Computed run by run for all valid runs of switch-closedloop-lowbw-v5 and switch-closedloop-perf-v1. P1 audio constant: the run-to-run median of the non-video link-layer rate (shaper sent bytes minus video packet link-layer bytes, divided by call duration) is between 55 and 70 kbps, and the coefficient of variation is less than 10%. P2 encoder floor: among runs where the median estimate after 15 seconds is below 80 kbps, the proportion of the main video payload rate falling between 26 and 38 kbps is no less than 90%. P3 baseline blind spot: among valid runs of the gcc arm at the two levels lowbw_156 and paper_low_200, the proportion of runs where the median estimate after 15 seconds is below 80 kbps is no less than two-thirds. If all three hold, it holds; if P1 or P2 does not hold, it does not hold; if only P3 does not hold, it is inconclusive (the sender-side conclusion holds but the baseline blind spot does not hold).

verdicts.basis: Post hoc inspection (not used as a criterion): among 84 non-crashing constant-capacity runs, the non-video link-layer rate had a median of 58.2 kbps, a coefficient of variation of 0.035, and a range of 56.0 to 64.1, with 50.8 packets per second and 142.9 bytes per packet, giving about 41 kbps after subtracting 42 bytes of link-layer overhead. The encoder floor was about 30 kbps, which maps to about 33 kbps at the link layer, and the two together total about 91 kbps. Thus the 100 kbps condition had only about 9 kbps of margin at the floor, the 156 kbps condition allowed at most about 93 kbps for video, and the 200 kbps condition allowed at most about 135 kbps. Median gcc estimates: 51.9, 56.1, and 80.0 for the 156 kbps condition; 67.8, 101.8, and 94.6 for the 200 kbps condition; and constantly about 280 for the 1000 and 2000 kbps conditions.
verdicts.limitations: P1's stability conclusion was restricted to non-crashed runs only after seeing the data, so it is a post hoc description. The audio constants hold only for this testbed's media configuration (test.wav, Opus default bitrate, one packet every 20 milliseconds). GCC is not entirely pinned at the floor, so it cannot be said that GCC has the same blind spot as ours, only that GCC is likewise constrained by the sender-side floor and audio occupancy under extremely low bandwidth.

question: Under the same measurement protocol as client-hardware-latency-energy, what are the p50, p95, p99, and maximum latency, single-inference net energy, and peak GPU memory of the full one-token LLM variant, the HCQ model (multi-scale encoder including unused modules, Qwen1.5-0.5B backbone and output head, randomly initialized with the same architecture), for a single inference on the local client GPU and on four CPU threads, and what are the corresponding values, in the same round, for the full LLM4Band system and for the two encoders alone?
criterion: Measurement only, no verdict, all readings reported. The protocol follows items 1–7 and item 10 of client-hardware-latency-energy unchanged: batch 1, 50 warm-up runs followed by 500 measured runs, synchronization before and after each run, report p50 p95 p99 and maximum, energy consumption minus idle baseline, record temperature, clock frequency and power source, report both VRAM variants, give headroom multiples relative to the measured decision interval (p50 120.17 ms, p95 242.61 ms). The input distribution is the per-dimension mean and standard deviation of MRE_4, regenerated for this run and archived with sha256. Validity gates (if any fails, the run is recorded as void and repeated): (1) all four arms are successfully constructed and fully measured on both GPU and CPU; (2) structural check: the parameter count of the HCQ encoder alone equals the encoder audit record of 515,088, and that of the full LLM4Band system differs from the first-version Full arm (464,670,872) by no more than 1; (3) when the GPU arm finishes measurement, SM frequency has dropped by no more than 15% relative to before measurement; (4) connect to external power. Predictions unfavorable to us: the smoke test shows the full HCQ model taking about twice as long on GPU as the full LLM4Band system, with the excess mainly in the encoder; on four-thread CPU, HCQ's p95 may approach or even exceed the 60 millisecond feedback period.

verdicts.basis: Full HCQ model: 465029287 parameters; four-thread CPU p50 42.054 p95 54.954 p99 64.105 ms; GPU p50 17.398 p95 18.061 ms, net energy 931.5 mJ, peak VRAM 1870.7 MiB. Per-arm readings are in the data event.
verdicts.limitations: Random initialization with the same architecture; latency, energy, and memory are independent of weight values. Only a single forward pass is measured, excluding state preprocessing, inter-process communication, and AlphaRTC integration. The local machine is a gaming laptop; results do not extrapolate to phones. There are no CPU energy numbers, and the sampling interval is longer than a single inference.

question: In the closed loop, is switch_nn no worse than the best arm and better than GCC, and does it fall into an under-use trap when the link is not saturated?
criterion: Thresholds are taken from noise-v1: utility 5.27, rate score 0.132. H1: on all four saturated low-bandwidth profiles, switch_nn utility is no less than the best fixed arm minus 5.27 (per profile); H2: on at least 3 of them, it beats gcc by at least 5.27; H3: on lowbw_1000 and paper_high_2000, switch_nn rate score is no less than the best fixed arm minus 0.132. If all three hold, it holds.

verdicts.basis: From cells.json and criteria.json: 100 valid runs, 44 collapsed cells. By profile: on the five profiles with capacity above 300 kbps, switch_nn is all valid and has no crash cells; against gcc it is higher by 20.0, 20.8, 15.3, 8.7, 12.2 in order, all exceeding the threshold 5.27; against the best fixed arm it is -0.05, -0.1, +2.7, -2.0, -8.4 in order, the first four within the threshold, and on the profile where saturated and unsaturated alternate switch_nn is the highest among all arms, with only paper_high_2000 trailing Schaferct_retrained by more than the threshold. On the three profiles with capacity 200 kbps and below, the learned arms almost all collapse, with gcc utility 55 to 63.
verdicts.limitations: 1. Results at 200 kbps and below are contaminated by defect 11 of the collector (main video stream and retransmission stream sequence numbers are mixed; replay evidence in switch-deploy-collector-v5), so they cannot be used to judge the true capability of the switcher or each arm at very low bandwidth and must be re-verified with the corrected collector. 2. gcc is the Python version of OpenNetLab; its estimate does not exceed 300 kbps, and above 300 kbps capacity it is nearly constant bitrate, so evidence for its advantage on these profiles is limited. 3. The metric is network utility, excluding video quality and freezing; latency uses the mean. 4. Single video source, approximately static. 5. The MLP arm collapses on all four profiles and partially collapses on the other two, making it the least safe arm in the closed loop, while it is the best single arm on offline macro MSE.

Holds: lower bound > 0 and Δ ≥ 0.10; direction only: Δ > 0; does not hold: Δ ≤ 0 or the LLM code throws exceptions in more than 5% of windows in any run. The LLM code is frozen on development runs only, with at most two rounds in which only error messages are returned. Unfavorable prediction: getStats has no per-packet latency, so all methods may have large deviations and differences may not be clear.

question: Does a locally run DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, reading the official feature descriptions, training data references, collector replay outputs, and source code, achieve higher feature-level F1 on 30 implanted variants than statistical detection without an LLM (KS with two thresholds and a ratio rule)?
criterion: Evaluation set, 33 frozen prompts (hash in prompts/SHA256SUMS.json starting with a51614c8), ground truth, statistical controls, and decision rules are identical to v1; only the main arm is replaced. Main arm: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, half precision, split across two V100S, sampling temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95 (officially recommended for this model), 3 independent samples per file, a limit of 32768 new tokens; reaching the limit without a final answer is recorded as truncation and counted as not detected, and the truncation count is reported separately. Report only: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (same settings) and the API outputs already produced in v1 (v4-pro 3 outputs, flash 11 outputs). Decision: the main arm holds if all differences for KS_0.2, KS_0.4, RATIO are not less than 0.05 and the interval lower bound is greater than 0; does not hold if any difference is not less than 0.05 and the interval upper bound is less than 0; otherwise inconclusive. Unfavorable prediction: the 14B distilled model reasons too weakly, its feature-level F1 cannot be distinguished from KS_0.2, and the truncation rate is high.

verdicts.basis: Main arm feature-level F1 0.595 (average of 3 samples, 99 outputs, 0 truncated); control F1 {"KS_0.2": 0.684, "KS_0.4": 0.704, "RATIO": 0.688, "PRIV_KS_VS_C": 0.474}; per control: KS_0.2 indistinguishable (difference -0.089, interval -0.183 to +0.001); KS_0.4 worse (difference -0.110, interval -0.186 to -0.037); RATIO worse (difference -0.093, interval -0.141 to -0.045); PRIV_KS_VS_C better (difference +0.120, interval +0.048 to +0.201). Real files detected individually (per sample): [{"collector_A.py": "1/9", "collector_B.py": "1/8", "collector_C.py": "1/1"}, {"collector_A.py": "1/9", "collector_B.py": "1/8", "collector_C.py": "1/1"}, {"collector_A.py": "0/9", "collector_B.py": "2/8", "collector_C.py": "1/1"}]. Report only arm F1: {"r1-distill-qwen-7b": 0.476, "qwen2.5-7b-instruct": 0.631}
verdicts.limitations: Category lists in the prompt benefit the LLM; implanted feature ground truth was set after viewing operator replay; only 3 real files; local 14B distilled model, half precision, sampling temperature 0.6; statistical comparison uses only short-window and long-window slot 0.

question: Does the feature-level F1 of the DeepSeek API model deepseek-flash (V4.1-Flash) on 30 implanted variants exceed that of statistical detection without an LLM (KS_0.2, KS_0.4, RATIO)?
criterion: Evaluation set, 33 frozen prompts (prompts/SHA256SUMS.json hash starting with a51614c8), ground truth, statistical controls, and decision rules are identical to v1 and v2; only the main arm is replaced with deepseek-flash (API default temperature, 3 independent samples per file, max_tokens 64000; an output truncated by length is archived and retried once, and if still truncated it counts as not detected). For the main arm, if all differences on KS_0.2, KS_0.4, and RATIO are no less than 0.05 and the interval lower bound is greater than 0, it holds; if any difference is no less than 0.05 and the interval upper bound is less than 0, it does not hold; otherwise it is inconclusive. Report only: per-item detection and report validity ratio for real files A, B, C, recall and precision for implanted subset items, PRIV and v2 local 14B readings. Pre-registration note: before registration, 11 sporadic flash outputs from v1 (per-item detection for collector_A, B, C and variant_00) and all 14B readings from v2 had already been seen; these outputs are not reused, all are rerun.

verdicts.basis: Main arm feature-level F1 0.720 (average of 3 samples, 0 truncated); control F1 {"KS_0.2": 0.684, "KS_0.4": 0.704, "RATIO": 0.688, "PRIV_KS_VS_C": 0.474}; per control: KS_0.2 indistinguishable (difference +0.036, interval +0.015 to +0.056); KS_0.4 indistinguishable (difference +0.015, interval -0.014 to +0.042); RATIO indistinguishable (difference +0.032, interval -0.033 to +0.093); PRIV_KS_VS_C better (difference +0.245, interval +0.128 to +0.358). question: What are the per-scenario four metrics for BoB and HRCC under the unified protocol, and can they be merged into the main table?
criterion: This is an export and evaluation, not a controlled experiment, and no criterion of superiority or inferiority is set. There are four mechanism gates; if any one fails, the result is void. First, the exported per-call step counts must match the lengths of arb_perstep_dump_v1 item by item, and the key order must also be the same. Second, after predicted values are converted to Mbps, the overall mean must fall between 0.05 and 8; otherwise it is judged that the unit or interface is misunderstood. Third, the proportion of non-finite values must be below one percent. Fourth, after merging into the main table, the self-check built into main_table_unified_v1 must still pass, that is, the relative differences of the three rows one-token LLM variant 6.743, Pioneer 7.37, and Schaferct-R 7.07 must not exceed 0.5%. Only if all four pass are the readings registered.

verdicts.basis: The keys and step counts for stepwise prediction are identical item by item to arb_perstep_dump_v1; means after conversion to Mbps: {"BoB": 1.2183986657573112, "HRCC": 0.9923975610558794, "GCC": 0.3009719824364386}. After merging, the main table per-scenario MSE (870): {"BoB": {"High BW": 45.8455, "Low BW": 0.865, "Fluctuating": 7.58, "macro": 18.0969}, "HRCC": {"High BW": 47.368, "Low BW": 213.3856, "Fluctuating": 279.2992, "macro": 180.0176}, "GCC": {"High BW": 58.1549, "Low BW": 0.1329, "Fluctuating": 9.7415, "macro": 22.6764}}
verdicts.limitations: The implementations and weights of the three estimators were taken from the original authors' directory and fed step by step with 150-dimensional observations using the same driver as their bundled calculate_metrics_bob; we did not retrain or tune, so these are reproduction readings of their public implementations and do not represent the tuned upper bounds of these methods. The rtc_env in the dependency chain was replaced in our own directory by a minimal shim generated by line-by-line truncation, retaining only the two conversion functions; the three removed import lines served only the Gym environment used for training, and the original file was not modified at all. Everything was run on CPU.

verdicts.basis: Tool error, data invalid (original conclusions retained in the event stream). GCC: the estimate adapter layer under the original author's directory validation/evaluate generates a batch of fake packets at each step, the clock restarts from zero, the delay gradient is 99.99% zero, the trend line is cleared before it can fill 20 packet groups, and the estimate stays at the initial value 300 kbps; out of 1.81 million steps, 87.2% are exactly 0.300, out of 870 calls, 663 calls are 0.3 throughout, and the three-cell MSE is nearly identical to the constant 0.3 (low bandwidth 0.1329 vs 0.1301). BoB: the adapter layer comments out half of the heuristic, line 245 substitutes the probability of the randomly selected action into the formula as bandwidth, sampling has no seed, and the output is independent of the input. HRCC: step_time is set to the interval between adjacent packets (median 12 ms, original design 200 ms), the reinforcement learning multiplier only rises and never falls, and out of 870 calls, 44 calls exceed 20 Mbps. The four gates only check key order, step count, mean interval, and non-finite values, so an output that is always 0.3 still passes all of them. The root cause was found in a read-only investigation on 2026-10-02 (40 files sampled on gpu-server-2 reproduced the original export bit for bit). The GCC and BoB rows of our earlier, unpublished manuscript are identical, cell for cell, to this export and are likewise invalid.
verdicts.limitations: After a minimal correction (packets accumulated across steps), GCC low-bandwidth MSE is 0.20 to 0.22; BoB and HRCC still diverge after correction; 150-dimensional replay cannot produce per-packet timing, and the three baselines are unusable on this path.

question: After fixing the two defects in online observation, does the per-feature distribution of the online observations return to the magnitude range of the offline training distribution, and do the two action-validity gates of v15 pass?
criterion: Written before the run. Defect one, clock basis: the receiver-side stats packetInfo.arrivalTimeMs is an absolute epoch millisecond measurement of 1789006661117, while header.sendTimestamp is an RTP timestamp measurement of 50528; the two use different bases, causing feature 4 mean delay minus baseline and feature 5 minimum delay to carry a raw offset of about 1.789e12; offline the same two dimensions take values no greater than 458 and 200 respectively. Defect two, rate units: online the receiving rate is computed with milliseconds as the denominator, yielding bits per millisecond, with a measured maximum of 149.733, while offline this feature is bits per second, below the median of the sub-0.3 Mbps bin, namely 78120, a 1000x difference. Decision one, distribution alignment: after correction, re-collect online observations, and for each of the 15 features the online maximum must not exceed 100 times the offline maximum of the same feature, and must not be below one hundredth of the offline maximum of the same feature; this gate checks all 15 features one by one, and if any one fails then decision one does not hold. Decision two, action effectiveness: with the corrected online path, rerun the three dynamic traces of v15 times 5 repetitions, and the two action gates, namely per-run action range greater than or equal to 50 kbit/s and median of p90 minus p10 greater than or equal to 30 kbit/s, must pass simultaneously. Decision three: the correction must be purely a units and basis correction, must not introduce any new features absent at training time, must not change feature definitions or order, and must not make any change to the model or weights; the online estimator code difference before and after correction must be line-by-line auditable. Only if all three decisions pass does it hold. If decision one passes but decision two does not, this is reported as such, with the explanation that the constant action has another cause.

verdicts.basis: Two defects are indeed fixed: the online maximum of the receiving rate feature changes from 149.733 to 147600, consistent with the offline bit/s scale; feature 4 changes from 1.789e12 to 479 versus offline 458, and feature 5 changes from 1.789e12 to 679 versus offline 200. Action validity is thereby restored: across 15 runs, the action range changes from 0.01 to 0.03 kbit/s before the fix to a minimum of 70.36, median 76.42, and maximum 88.96 kbit/s, the median of p90 minus p10 changes from 0.01 to 45.15 kbit/s, and the median action range is 76.48 to 153.09 kbit/s. Macro utility improves by 118.9769% relative to a 240 kbit/s fixed controller, CI95 [102.8347, 134.5494], with the three traces at +145.861%, +86.519%, and +124.551% respectively.
verdicts.limitations: 1. The failure of decision 1 is substantially due to our criterion design: it used the offline global maximum as the reference, and that maximum is dominated by high-bandwidth calls, making it too strict for this testbed, which can only run at about 200 kbit/s; the four failures, 3, 7, 8, and 9, are structural because each monitoring interval contains only 1 packet, so packet interval and jitter cannot be computed. The criterion is not relaxed post hoc; the gate should later be redefined with reference to the offline distribution at the same capacity. 2. The RTP timestamp contains no absolute one-way delay information, so features 4 and 5 still have an overall shift by an unknown constant relative to the training distribution, and this fix cannot eliminate it. 3. The fix takes effect only inside the local container; any online deployment on the server is unaffected and has not been synchronized. 4. The seven gates were passed with four CPU threads and an inference p95 of 64.60 milliseconds, and this cannot be extrapolated to GPU deployment.

question: If D5's shrinkage gate is transferred to the interface that outputs 15 tokens, how much does the three-seed mean macro MSE improve relative to the no-gate baseline on the same interface, and is this gain larger than, comparable to, or smaller than the 3.517% that D5 achieved on the no-LLM lightweight arm?
criterion: Fixed before the run; the verdict follows criteria-amendment-v2. All three arms output [bs,15,1024] fed into the base_model of Qwen1.5-0.5B, take the last token of last_hidden_state into BweHead, token-for-token identical to the existing MultiToken arm; all parameters except the encoder are identical and consistent with the 50k protocol of llm_value: MRE_4, batch 512, buffer_size 3500000, max_timesteps 50000, eval_freq 5000, the only endpoint at step 50000, seeds 0, 1, 2, three arms times three seeds for nine runs. T-A0 is a per-feature Linear(10,1024) generating 15 tokens, no gate, as baseline; T-D5 is the same per-feature projection plus the scalar gate of D5, the gate input is the full 150 dimensions, the shrinkage target is 15 per-token learnable priors; T-MT is the existing MultiToken encoder, as anchor to link back to the published result of MT improving 3.406% over SmallTransformer. Per-token priors are mandatory rather than optional: if the 15 tokens share one prior, when the gate is closed the 15 tokens will be completely identical, attention degrades again in the low-bandwidth region where the gate is closed, and that is exactly the scenario where D5 most needs it to work. The primary adjudication targets T-D5 relative to T-A0, four groups per criteria-amendment-v2: group A is that for seed0 the 95% CI of the 870-call paired bootstrap (10000 resamples, seed 20260909) lies entirely below 0, and on the 712-call leakage-free subset the direction is the same and the CI is maintained; group B is that all three seeds agree in direction and the 95% confidence interval of the three-seed mean excludes 0 by a t distribution with 2 degrees of freedom; group C is tiered, at least 3% recorded as definitive contribution, at least 1.631% recorded as a reportable positive result; group D is that macro increase caused by deterioration in any scenario does not exceed 1%. Parallel to the primary adjudication, the theoretical adjudication must be answered and was already derived before the run from three measurements: (1) Qwen's terminal RMSNorm makes the output norm constant at 32.0000, after scaling the input up 3 times the output norm is unchanged, so the overall scale is completely erased, and any scalar-scaling-type gate fails in principle when connected to an LLM; (2) direction changes can pass through, after changing the input from v to 0.2v plus 0.8p the output cosine drops to 0.1681, D5's gate is direction interpolation because the prior is nonzero, so its signal can propagate; (3) with 15 tokens changing the first 14 tokens makes the output cosine of the last token become 0.5682, proving that attention is indeed reading other tokens, whereas with a single token this channel does not exist. Accordingly the theoretical prediction is: because self-attention itself provides input-dependent aggregation, overlapping with the gate's function, the gain of T-D5 relative to T-A0 should be smaller than D5's 3.517% on the no-LLM arm. If the measured gain stays at that level or is larger, then this theoretical prediction is falsified, and it must be reported as is and reinterpreted; it must not be claimed after the fact that both are correct. Secondary readings are reported as they are, without a gate: the improvement of T-MT relative to T-A0; the gate value distributions of the three arms, where if the gap of T-D5's gate across scenarios is significantly smaller than 0.564 on the no-LLM arm, then it supports the explanation that attention already bears part of the adaptive function. Risks: (1) the last token corresponds to feature 14, the probing packet proportion, whose median absolute value on the training set is exactly 0, so using it as the readout position may be unfavorable, but the existing MT arm does so and has already passed, so it is kept unchanged; (2) the per-feature Linear(10,1024) differs from the conference encoder's Linear(150,1024), the former sees only one feature per token, so T-A0 is not an equivalent of the conference encoder and can only serve as an internal baseline under the same interface, and must not be used for direct comparison with the conference version; (3) each of the nine runs has about 460 million parameters, and about 7.4 GiB of memory per run had been measured earlier. Criteria are not changed after the run, checkpoints are not selected, and results are not reported only for favorable arms or favorable seeds.

verdicts.basis: 50k fixed endpoint, T-D5 three-seed average macro 6.413633, T-A0 6.363039, improvement -0.795%, seed0 paired CI95 [-0.26929806347556173, -0.04647955381808661], theoretical prediction not falsified.
verdicts.limitations: Two risks listed before the run are recorded here as written, with no post hoc justification: First, the last token corresponds to feature 14, the probing packet proportion; the median absolute value of this feature on the training set is exactly 0, so using it as the readout position may be unfavorable, but the existing MT arm does so and has already achieved passing results, so it is kept consistent without change. Second, the per-feature Linear(10,1024) differs from the conference encoder's Linear(150,1024); the former lets each token see only one feature, so T-A0 is not an equivalent of the conference encoder and can only serve as an internal baseline under the same interface, and must not be used for direct comparison with the conference version. Also: this round ran only two arms (plan B) and the T-MT anchor arm was postponed, so the results can only be compared with each other and must not be asserted to be on the same scale as the published MT improvement of 3.406% relative to SmallTransformer; a later run of the anchor arm is recorded as a continuation and does not reopen this verdict.

verdicts.basis: All 870 validation calls are within the 941 held-out set, with 0 calls in the training set; the two directories do not overlap, totaling 9405. MRE_4 has 3500000 entries, of which 3483935 are distinct; all match (0 unmatched), 47660 entries have multiple identical sources, of which 72 also have identical copies in held-out calls, but after source selection all sources are in the training set (0 in the held-out set); all 8464 training calls have samples. After reconstruction by index, the six fields observations, actions, next_observations, rewards, terminals, true_capacitys are bitwise identical to MRE_4; each bin has 500000 entries (3 to 4 Mb/s is empty), with 1444 missing-capacity entries. Conclusion: MRE_4 can be bitwise reconstructed from public calls plus indices; the earlier document's statement that "the 8464 training manifest was not saved" is incorrect.
verdicts.limitations: Exploratory results, not paper evidence; confirmatory experiments designed from them must use new data.
